name: Lowering Breath
description: Breathe slowly while a small stream of qi is led through a bruise or strain to ease it in yourself or an ally.

name: Qi Thread
description: Narrow a pinch of qi to a thin line and snap it from the fingertip so it stings the target.

name: Pulse Jab
description: Time a straight jab to the beat of the pulse so a short burst of qi lands with the knuckles.

name: Rooted Breath
description: Sink the breath low and spread qi through legs and trunk so a push meets a firm body that gives no ground.

name: Breath Stride
description: Draw a breath and send qi to the legs for one long stride that closes or opens the gap.

name: Reserve Count
description: Count the pulse and the breath to feel how much qi remains in the dantian and how evenly it moves.

name: Circuit Palm
description: Run qi from the dantian down the arm and back so the open palm lands with the whole loop behind it.

name: Joined Loop
description: Keep qi circling through both forearms so crossed arms take a blow as one braced and humming guard.

name: Loop Pace
description: Let the circuit carry qi into the lead leg so the step lands lightly and the back foot follows fast.

name: Flow Check
description: Press two fingers to the wrist and follow the circuit to find where qi runs thin or stalls in yourself.

name: Palm Wave
description: Push both palms out together and release the stored loop as a broad soft wave that shoves those ahead.

name: Ring Press
description: Close a ring of fingers on a target's wrist and press qi into it until the grip weakens.

name: Gather Palm
description: Gather qi into one palm for a slow count and strike so the stored weight lands at once.

name: Gathered Shot
description: Pack qi into a fist-sized ball in the palm and throw it a short way at the target.

name: Held Pool
description: Hold qi pooled in the dantian without spending it so your next strike or guard lands with extra force.

name: Pool Guard
description: Draw the pooled qi out to the skin in a still layer that absorbs the first force of a hit.

name: Slow Release
description: Let gathered qi seep into a wounded limb of yourself or an ally a little at a time to dull pain.

name: Cupped Strike
description: Cup the palm and slap so the held qi bursts inward on contact and rattles the body behind it.

name: Mild Surge
description: Let the gathered qi surge outward from both hands in a short push that knocks back close foes.

name: Pulse Palm
description: Strike with an open palm on the instant the heartbeat peaks so qi and blow arrive together.

name: Double Pulse
description: Throw two quick strikes on two beats so the second drives qi deeper through the first's mark.

name: Pulse Knock
description: Tap a pulse of qi into the elbow or wrist so a held weapon or guard loosens.

name: Pulse Swerve
description: Meet an incoming strike with a small beat of qi in the forearm and turn it wide.

name: Pulse Slip
description: Slide off the line of a blow on the off-beat with qi in the hips and ankles.

name: Pulse Scan
description: Feel the rhythm of a nearby body through your own pulse to know when it will move.

name: Level Tempo
description: Level the qi in every channel so strength feeds all limbs alike and your next movements come with less strain.

name: Flow Cut
description: Draw the edge of the hand across the target in one flowing stroke carrying a thin sheet of qi.

name: Flow Turn
description: Let qi pour along the arm and turn it like a wheel so an incoming blow slides away.

name: Flow Slide
description: Slide the feet on a smooth current of qi to shift sideways without breaking the guard.

name: Flow Mend
description: Guide an even current of qi through a strained muscle of yourself or an ally until it unknots.

name: Flow Lock
description: Stop the flow in a grabbed arm with a pinch of qi so the limb stiffens for a few breaths.

name: Qi Shroud
description: Spread a thin skin of qi over the whole body so blows land softer and cuts bite less.

name: Forearm Ward
description: Pack qi hard into one forearm and raise it to take a heavy blow on the bone.

name: Shoulder Brace
description: Set the shoulder and run qi into it so a charge or tackle stops against it.

name: Glancing Veil
description: Angle the veil of qi at the point of impact so a strike glances away rather than lands.

name: Veil Mend
description: Fold the veil of qi round a bruised spot on yourself or an ally and hold it warm until the swelling eases.

name: Riposte Pulse
description: Answer a blocked blow with a returning beat of qi through the guard arm into the striker.

name: Thread Feeling
description: Spin a fine thread of qi out of the hand and read through it the body it touches.

name: Thread Probe
description: Send a single thread into the ground or a wall to learn what stirs close behind it.

name: Hairline Thread
description: Draw qi to a hair-thin point at two fingers and drive it through a gap in armor or cloth.

name: Thread Cinch
description: Loop qi threads around a wrist or ankle and draw them taut to hold the limb still.

name: Thread Twang
description: Pluck a taut thread of qi against a foe's guard arm so the muscle jerks and the guard breaks.

name: Drawn Thread
description: Tie a thread of qi between yourself and an ally and tighten it so both move in the same rhythm.

name: Light Step
description: Lift the heel on a breath of qi so the body skips forward a short distance almost silent.

name: Springing Step
description: Coil qi into the calves then spring up and away from a low sweep or grab.

name: Side Slip
description: Shift the weight and throw a thread of qi to the far foot to slip to the side in a single motion.

name: Quiet Foot
description: Soften each footfall with a cushion of qi so a walking Warrior makes no sound on stone or leaf.

name: Breath Hop
description: Exhale sharply while kicking off so the hop clears a low obstacle and lands balanced.

name: Mending Exhale
description: Breathe in time with an ally while qi flows through the hurt place and eases bruise and ache.

name: Easing Palm
description: Rest a palm warmed with qi on the injured body of yourself or a companion to calm swelling and tremor.

name: Easing Flow
description: Open a stiff channel in yourself or an ally with slow circling qi so strained limbs move freely again.

name: Quiet Beat
description: Hold a companion's wrist and read their pulse to learn where the hurt lies and how deep.

name: Rest Breath
description: Take three still breaths that return wind and strength to yourself so the next exchange begins fresh.

name: Soothe Wave
description: Pass one soft wave of qi through an ally's chest to settle the heart after a hard blow.

name: Knit Thread
description: Stitch the edges of a shallow cut in yourself or an ally with fine qi threads so it stops weeping.

name: Pressure Palm
description: Compress qi in the palm until it hums and strike so the pressure bursts into the target.

name: Hard Release
description: Hold the pressure to the last moment then let it all go through the heel of the hand.

name: Wave Knock
description: Stamp and release the compressed qi as a ring of force that pushes back all within a stride.

name: Press Hold
description: Bear down with a steady push of qi on a foe's shoulder until the arm sags and the stance drops.

name: Drive Palm
description: Plant the lead foot and thrust the loaded palm forward so the foe is driven back a pace.
